Description: I have lived at this address since February 2011 and have always paid the rent each month.  The owners (now the husband is deceased as of this year) live in England 6 months out of the year and Nokomis Florida for Florida's season for 6 months.  They have made "moderate" repairs on the property and have always (for the most part) left it up to me to take care of the problems, - in other words, I would need to take off work, etc.  I would then deduct it from my rent. I found out in 2014 that Mr. Morgan had cancer and out of respect only bothered them regarding major repairs such as when the bathroom faucets rusted off (I needed to use a screwdriver to turn them on and when the air conditioning stopped working).  Prior to that repairs were done by Mr. Morgan and his neighbor.  One such example was the air conditioning ducts under the house.  One of the major ones had fallen and there was no air blowing into the home.  He and his neighbor came out and replaced 3 of them.  Mr. Morgan only did the absolute minimum that was needed.Currently there is no air coming into the back bathroom, very little out of the back bedroom and half capacity in the living and kitchen areas.  My electric bills in the summer run around $275.00 per month for a 2 bedroom mobile home. I did, though, write an email to Mrs. Morgan in 2014 explaining that the mobile home was in dire need of a new roof due to it leaking in 3 places as well as the fact that two windows had broken in the "open" position and the most important at the time was the shower handles in the bathroom had rotted off and I was having to use a pair of pliers.  After 3 months I was given permission over a 2 month period (I was not allowed to use the rent money to fix it all at once but to split it between 2 months).Mrs. Morgan informed me that when they arrived in the 2015/2016 season she would insure the repairs were made "even if she had to fix them herself".  Upon arriving, I was told how much they enjoyed me as a tenant and they would be selling the property and I was to cooperate with the real estate agent.  I prepared a list for the agent of everything that was wrong with the house.  As a result, the agent dropped the sale and would not list the property. I was told by Mrs. Morgan that I could stay until October of 2016.   I suppose I've gotten off track and this is really all that you needed to know.  So, please find below the property details:There is no electricity in the small bathroom that faces the driveway.  There is no electricity in the "master bath" other then the lights work. I brush my teeth in the kitchen and dry my hair in the bedroom.   The front window is broken and I had to nail it shut.  The window in the kitchen is broken open and will not close at all.  The roof is leaking in the living room, kitchen, washer/dryer area and a small amount in the back bedroom.  The stove does not work other than the burners.  The sinks leak under the kitchen and master bath.  The handle that turns the water on and off in the master bath rusted off.  There are many roaches.  The bedroom that faces the driveway the floor has dropped out under the carpet, the faucet in the kitchen leaks.  You can see under the house through holes in the floor where the floors meet the walls.  I believe this is it, but can update when I get the paper I did for the realtor.  I have copies of emails, etc., copies of the rent being paid, etc.

Description: We have owned the vacant residential lot located at 9308 Arnaz Circle since 2003 in anticipation of our retirement in 2019. Since we reside 2.5 hours away in Broward County, we make periodic visits to our property to check on its condition. Approximately two years ago, we visited and realized that the neighbor at 9300 Arnaz Circle was parking a utility trailer and a large Class A recreational vehicle on our property, immediately adjacent to their property. In addition, these folks stored miscellaneous gardening items and other things typically found in ones garage. We communicated with the owners at 9300 Arnaz Circle regarding our request to have them remove the vehicles and items. Our request was met with a discourteous response. Most important to us was the outcome that these folks moved the vehicles to the vacant lot directly across the street from their home and off our property. Case closed&or so we thought.On June 20, 2017, I again inspected our property and discovered that the neighbors were now parking the large RV as well as a red PT Cruiser sedan in the public right-of-way directly in front of our property. The utility trailers were now parked on the lot across from 9300 Arnaz Circle. I know that these vehicles belong to the folks at 9300 Arnaz as I am familiar with the vehicles and trailers. While there, the lady from 9300 confronted me while I was in my vehicle documenting the situation. Knowing her potential for vitriol and discourtesy, coupled with her apparent angry non-verbal posturing, I decided to drive away rather than provoke a senseless confrontation. Because I suffer from impaired vocals, I asked my wife to telephone these folks and kindly (again) request that they remove their vehicles from our property.  My wife reported that the man (and woman) were again belligerent and discourteous when informed of our simple request to have them relocate their vehicles. The man reportedly stated that he would keep the RV parked where it was until the wheels fall off (or something to that effect). He berated us and our request. I informed my wife to cease any further communication since our attempts to resolve these issues informally were futile.Ive got a pretty good understanding of laws and ordinances so I conducted a review of Charlotte Countys Code of Ordinances. My review revealed possible code violations that exist in this situation that we hope can possibly if applicable be leveraged to get these folks to comply with our simple request. CCCO 3-9-79.1 contains a variety of what I believe are applicable subsections. Specifically:3-9-79.1(d) states that in residential districts RVs must be parked upon property owned by the vehicle owner and parked behind the leading edge of the residential structure and upon a paved driveway;3-9-79.1(e) states that RV parking is prohibited upon the public right-of-way or any vacant property or any portion thereof.  I apologize for having to resort to bringing you good people into this situation, so Ive provided great detail in my summary to let you know that this strategy of getting government involved was our option of last resort. In addition, I expect retaliation from these folks in some form or fashion so I request that your inspector evaluate my property for any issues which constitute violations or need attending. It should be noted that in their June 20th conversation, the man from 9300 threatened to have us cited for having Brazilian Pepper Trees on our property. If there are in fact any conditions that represent code or other violations, you have my promise that I will respond quickly to correct them. Please feel free to call or email me if you have any comments or concerns.Thank you in advance,Larry mrav8r@mindspring.com 954-931-3374I have attached two photos, one is an aerial from the County GIS which shows the previous situation as well as a photo that I took on June 20, 2017 which reflects the current situation.

There are major support beams and girders that are completely rotted away. There are numerous locations on exterior of building missing siding and even wall structure. On the rear of the house the entire exterior wall appears to be on the brink of falling off building completely. There are loose wires sticking out of exterior walls, interior walls and hanging everywhere underneath building. There is a shower drain that has no plumbing at all underneath the sub flooring. There are multiple plumbing fixtures with little to no support underneath them. One toilet in particular is on the verge of falling through floor into basement below. Until recently when the septic system was replaced, the waste/drain line was ran into adjacent lot and collected in a hole that was dug and covered with a tarp. there is still remanents of the tarp and waste. The entire area smells of feces and urine. There are no functions AC units in building at all. They were replaced with wall unit on all three rear lanais. There is mold growing everywhere and drywall plaster and paint are falling off everywhere as well. There is squishy patches of drywall that have hidden years of pipe leaks and neglect. There are multiple walls missing where studs rotted away and were spliced with other pieces of lumber and then covered with plywood. There are columns on front porches missing and there is nothing supporting the roof in front of house. Parts of the awnings and eves have fell off and are on the verge of falling through garage ceiling. There are multiple holes and weak spots in roof. There are no rails, guards or spindles on any of the front porches. In my opinion the entire building is beyond repair and should be condemned.
